title: 2026-27 UK public-sector sustainability and GHG reporting QA controls

facts.source_fact: HM Treasury published Sustainability Reporting Guidance 2026-27 on 16 July 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Attach reporting-year vintage to public-sector disclosures.

facts.source_fact: The 2026-27 guidance supports sustainability reporting in central government annual reports and accounts.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the central-government reporting boundary before downstream use.

facts.source_fact: The guidance may also be used by other public sector bodies.
facts.expected_handling: Distinguish mandatory central-government use from wider optional applicability.

facts.source_fact: The 2026-27 publication sets minimum sustainability-reporting requirements for the reporting year.
facts.expected_handling: Separate minimum requirements from additional voluntary disclosures.

facts.source_fact: The 2026-27 guidance also addresses reporting requirements and considerations where sustainability information is material.
facts.expected_handling: Apply materiality explicitly to information beyond minimum requirements.

facts.source_fact: For 2026-27, general principles, concepts and foundations are consolidated into a separate appendix.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve document hierarchy between annual requirements and foundational guidance.

facts.source_fact: The 2026-27 publication points users to the Government Financial Reporting Manual for wider public-sector reporting context.
facts.expected_handling: Keep sustainability reporting aligned with the applicable financial-reporting framework.

facts.source_fact: The 2026-27 publication points users to TCFD-aligned application guidance for public-sector climate disclosure context.
facts.expected_handling: Do not merge TCFD and SRG metrics without an explicit mapping.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance states that from 2026-27 central government bodies are expected to comply with the guidance or explain non-compliance, subject to conflicts with other mandatory reporting frameworks.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve transition wording and conflict exceptions.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance strengthened emphasis on data quality in integrated sustainability reporting.
facts.expected_handling: Carry data-quality provenance into reported GHG figures.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance strengthened emphasis on proportionality.
facts.expected_handling: Apply proportionality without omitting mandatory minimum disclosures.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance strengthened alignment between sustainability and financial reporting boundaries.
facts.expected_handling: Require a boundary reconciliation when sustainability and financial scopes differ.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance streamlined minimum reporting requirements around a smaller set of core environmental metrics.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer that non-core information is prohibited where material.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance clarified reporting thresholds and exemptions.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the relevant threshold before assigning disclosure requirements.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance introduced a comply-or-explain basis for specified sustainability disclosures.
facts.expected_handling: Record an explanation when a required disclosure is not provided rather than silently treating it as zero.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance includes minimum reporting requirements for Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse-gas emissions.
facts.expected_handling: Keep Scope 1 and Scope 2 values separately identified before aggregation.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance uses a materiality-based approach to Scope 3 greenhouse-gas emissions.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat Scope 3 as universally mandatory or universally optional without materiality assessment.

facts.source_fact: The 2025-26 guidance states there is no minimum Scope 3 reporting requirement, but related information should be reported where material.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve the distinction between minimum requirements and material additional disclosure.

facts.source_fact: The guidance identifies baseline information such as fuel use, mileage, electricity and gas consumption and raw-material use as inputs to GHG accounting.
facts.expected_handling: Keep activity data and emission-conversion steps traceable.

facts.source_fact: The guidance describes converting baseline information to CO2e using emission factors and recognises both emissions as they occur and embodied emissions already incurred.
facts.expected_handling: Label conversion-factor vintage and distinguish operational from embodied-emissions views.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact and its reporting-year wording without broadening scope.
Attach entity, reporting boundary and emissions scope before downstream use.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents mixing public-sector scopes or reporting frameworks.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach reporting year and publication/update date, especially across the 2025-26 to 2026-27 transition.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents stale-vintage requirements being applied silently.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry source URL, activity-data basis, conversion-factor provenance and materiality method into derived outputs.
Do not convert public-sector organisational disclosures into parcel-level measured emissions without a separate parcel-binding gate.
